title: THE BEAUTY OF RELYING ON GOD [WHEN YOU LET GO, GOD TAKES OVER]
text: I want you to [music] open your Bible with me to the book of Proverbs chapter 3 from verse 5. The Bible says, "Trust in the [music] Lord with all thine heart and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him and he shall direct thy path." Somebody shout hallelujah. You see, there is [music] a dimension of divine intervention that only becomes activated when human [music] effort ceases. There is a realm of God's manifestation that remains dormant until man comes to the end of himself. [music] The scripture is replete with examples of men and women who discovered that the greatest breakthroughs in their lives came not when they were struggling, not when they [music] were fighting in their own strength, but when they surrendered completely to the lordship and the [music] supremacy of Jehovah. I have come to discover that one of the greatest tests of spiritual maturity is the ability to [music] trust God when everything around you is screaming for you to take control. The carnal mind, the Adamic nature always wants to be in charge. It always wants [music] to have a backup plan. It always wants to keep something in reserve. But I have come to tell you tonight that there is a beauty, there is a glory, there is a manifestation that comes [music] when you completely let go and allow God to take over. When I say [music] let go, I'm not talking about irresponsibility. I'm not talking about laziness. I'm not talking about folding your hands and doing nothing. No, I'm talking about that place where you [music] have done all you know to do. You have exhausted human wisdom. You have deployed [music] human strategy and you come to a place of complete surrender where you say, "Lord, if you don't show [music] up, I'm finished. If you don't intervene, there is no other way." The children of Israel at the Red Sea experienced [music] this dimension. When they got to the Red Sea with Pharaoh's army behind them, mountains on either side, and water [music] before them, they had nowhere to go. They had come to the end of human [music] possibility. And it was at that junction, at that critical moment that Moses said something very profound. He says, "Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord. Stand still. Stop panicking. Stop trying to figure it out. Stop looking [music] for human solutions. Just stand still and watch God work." You [music] see beloved, when you are always busy trying to fix things, when you are always scheming, when you [music] are always manipulating circumstances, you rob God of the opportunity to demonstrate his power in your life. There are some battles you are not supposed to fight. There are some situations [music] you are not supposed to fix. Your assignment is to pray, to trust, to believe, and to watch God work. I remember when Abraham was told [music] by God to offer Isaac as a sacrifice. This was the son of promise. The son that came after 25 [music] years of waiting. The son through whom all the promises of God were supposed to be fulfilled. And God said, [music] "Take him to Mount Mariah and offer him as a burnt offering." Now, humanly speaking, this made no sense. How can you kill the son [music] of promise and still expect the promise to be fulfilled? But Abraham had learned something about God. He had learned that God is faithful. [music] He had learned that God cannot lie. He had learned that even if he killed Isaac, [music] God was able to raise him from the dead. So Abraham took Isaac, built an altar, arranged the wood, bound his [music] son, and lifted up the knife. And at that moment when he had [music] completely let go, when he had demonstrated total obedience, when he had shown that he trusted [music] God more than he trusted his own understanding, the angel of the Lord appeared and said,"Abraham, Abraham, do not lay your hand on [music] the lad, for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me." And the Bible records something very powerful. It says Abraham [music] lifted up his eyes and looked and behold behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. You see, the ram was already there. God had already made provision, but Abraham [music] could not see the ram until he was willing to let go of Isaac. There are provisions in your life that you cannot see because you [music] are holding on too tightly to what you have. There are open doors that you cannot access because you are refusing to surrender completely to God. Let me take you to the New Testament. the feeding of the 5,000. Jesus had been ministering to a multitude and evening came and the people were hungry. The disciples came to Jesus and said, "Send them away so [music] they can go to the surrounding villages and buy food." But Jesus said something that seemed impossible. He said, "You give [music] them something to eat." The disciples were shocked. They said, "Shall we go and buy 200 dinary [music] worth of bread and give them to eat?" They were thinking in human terms, calculating [music] with human wisdom, reasoning with cannal understanding. But then Andrew came forward with [music] a little boy who had five bal loaves and two small fish. Andrew said, "There [music] is a lad here who has five bales and two fish. But what are they among so many?" You see in the hands of that little boy, those loaves and fishes were just launched. They were insignificant. [music] They were not enough. But something happened when that little boy let go. When he released what he [music] had into the hands of Jesus, when he stopped holding on to his provision and surrendered it completely, Jesus took it, blessed it, broke it, and it multiplied to feed 5,000 men besides women and children with 12 baskets left over. This is what I have come to tell you tonight. What you are holding on to that business idea, that relationship, that career, that dream, that ambition in your hands, it will remain limited. In [music] your hands, it will remain small. In your hands, it will remain insufficient. But when you let go and give it to Jesus, when you surrender it completely to God, he will take it. [music] He will bless it. He will break it. And he will multiply it beyond your imagination. [music] Open your Bible with me to the book of Exodus chapter 14. I want to show you something about [music] the nature of God. When the children of Israel were trapped at the Red Sea, the Bible says, "The [music] Lord said to Moses, why do you cry to me? Tell the children of Israel to go forward, but lift up [music] your rod and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, and the children of Israel shall go on dry ground through the midst of the sea." Now, [music] watch this carefully. God said, "Stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it." He didn't say, "I will divide the sea." He said, "You divide it." But [music] Moses understood something. He understood that he could not divide the sea in his own strength. He understood that the power to divide the sea was [music] not in his arm, but in his obedience. So Moses stretched out his hand not because he believed in his own ability, but because he believed in God's command. He let go of his fear. He let go of his doubt. He let go of [music] human reasoning. And when he stretched out his hand in faith, God sent a [music] strong east wind that blew all night and divided the waters. [music] And the children of Israel crossed over on dry ground. This is the principle I want you to understand tonight. Your obedience is the trigger for God's intervention. Your surrender is the key that unlocks divine provision. Your willingness to let go is the signal that releases God's power. As long [music] as you are holding on, as long as you are trusting in your own wisdom, as long as you are [music] depending on your own strength, God will wait. But the moment you let go, the moment you surrender, the moment you say, "God, I cannot do this without you." That is when heaven moves. That is when angels are dispatched. That is when [music] miracles happen. I want to take you to the book of 2 Kings chapter 4. There was a widow who came to Elisha in distress. Her husband who was one of the sons of the prophets had died [music] and the creditor was coming to take her two sons as slaves to pay off the debt. She cried [music] out to Elisha, "Your servant, my husband, is dead and you know that your servant feared the Lord and the creditor is [music] coming to take my two sons to be his slaves." Elisha asked her a very important question. He said, "What do you have in your house?" She said, "Your [music] maid servant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil." Now, she said she had nothing but then she [music] mentioned that she had a jar of oil. You see, sometimes what you think is nothing is the seed for your miracle. Sometimes [music] what you are despising is the very thing God wants to use to turn your situation around. Elisha gave her [music] very specific instructions. He said, "Go borrow vessels from everywhere, from all your neighbors, empty vessels. Do not gather, just a few. And when you have come in, you shall shut the door behind you and your sons. Then pour it into all those vessels and set aside the full ones." Now watch what happened. The Bible says, "She [music] went from Elisha and shut the door behind her and her sons who brought the vessels to her, and she [music] poured it out. The oil kept flowing and flowing and flowing until all the vessels were full. And when she said, "Bring me another vessel." Her son said to her, "There is not another vessel." And then the oil ceased. Can you see the principle? The oil flowed as long as there were vessels to receive it. The miracle was limited not by God's supply, but by her capacity to receive. And notice something very important. Before the miracle happened, she had to do something. She had to let go of her pride and go borrow vessels from her neighbors. She had to let go of her embarrassment and ask for help. She had to let go of her fear [music] of judgment and obey the prophet's instruction. And it was her willingness to let go, her willingness [music] to obey, her willingness to step out in faith that activated the supernatural. This is what I have come to tell you. Your breakthrough is [music] connected to your obedience. Your miracle is tied to your willingness to let go and trust God. As [music] long as you are holding on to your reputation, as long as you are afraid of what people will say, as long as you are unwilling to step out of your comfort zone, the oil will not flow. The miracle will not manifest. The breakthrough [music] will not come. But when you let go, when you surrender your pride, when you release [music] your fear, when you stop caring about the opinions of men and start caring about the will of God, [music] that is when heaven opens. That is when the supernatural invades the natural. That is when impossibilities [music] become possibilities. Take your Bible to the Gospel of John chapter 11. This is the story of Lazarus. Lazarus was sick and his sisters Mary and Martha sent word to Jesus saying, "Lord, behold he whom [music] you love is sick." Now the Bible says Jesus loved [music] Martha and her sister and Lazarus. But when he heard that Lazarus was sick, he stayed two more days in the place where he was. This seems strange, doesn't it? If he loved them, why didn't [music] he rush to heal Lazarus? Why did he deliberately delay? By the time Jesus arrived in Bethany, Lazarus had been in the tomb for 4 days. Martha [music] came to meet Jesus and said, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died." There was pain in her voice. There was disappointment. [music] There was confusion. She had trusted Jesus. She had believed in his power. But he didn't come in time. He didn't show up when she expected him to. But Jesus said something [music] very profound. He said, "Your brother will rise again." Martha thought he was talking about the resurrection at the last day. But Jesus said, "I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me, though he may die, [music] he shall live. And whoever lives and believes in me shall never die." Do you believe this? And Martha said, "Yes, [music] Lord. They believe that you are the Christ, the son of God who is to come into the world. Now watch what happened next. Jesus went to the tomb and said, "Take away the stone." Martha protested. She said, "Lord, by this time there [music] is a stench, for he has been dead 4 days." She was operating in natural reasoning. She was thinking [music] with human understanding. She was looking at the situation from a cannal perspective. But Jesus said to her, "Did I not say to you that if you would believe, you would see the glory of God?" They took away the stone. Jesus lifted up [music] his eyes and said, "Father, I thank you that you have heard me, and I know that you always hear me." But because of the people who are standing by, I said this that they may believe that you sent me. And when he had said these things, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he who had died came out bound hand and foot with grave [music] clothes, and his face was wrapped with a cloth. Jesus said to them, "Lose him and let him go." Can you see what happened here? Mary and Martha had to let go of their expectations. They had to let go of their timeline. [music] They had to let go of their understanding of how God should work. They thought Jesus [music] should have come immediately to heal Lazarus. But God had a bigger plan. God wanted to do something greater than healing. He wanted to [music] demonstrate resurrection power. He wanted to show that he's not bound by natural laws. He wanted to prove that nothing [music] is impossible with him. And this is what I have come to tell you tonight. Sometimes God will deliberately [music] delay your breakthrough because he wants to do something bigger than you are asking for. Sometimes he will allow the situation to [music] get worse because he wants to demonstrate a greater glory. Sometimes he will let things die because he wants to show you resurrection power. But you have to let go. You have [music] to let go of your timeline. You have to let go of your expectations. You have to let go [music] of your limited understanding of how God should work. When you let go and trust him completely, when you surrender your will to his will, when you stop trying to dictate to God how he should answer your prayers, that is [music] when you position yourself to see his glory. I want you to understand something very important tonight. Faith is not [music] just believing that God can. Faith is believing that God will even when you cannot [music] see how. Faith is trusting God's character when you cannot trace his hand. Faith is holding on [music] to his promises when everything around you contradicts those promises. Faith is letting go of your control and giving God complete authority over your life. The book of Proverbs 16:9 [music] says, "A man's heart plans his way, but the Lord directs his steps." You can make all the plans you want. You can strategize all you want. You can scheme all you want. But [music] ultimately, it is God who directs your steps. It is God who orders your path. It is God who determines the outcome. So why waste your energy fighting? Why exhaust yourself struggling? Why burden yourself with anxiety and worry when you can simply let go and let [music] God take over? Let me tell you what happens when you let go. When you let go, you enter into rest. The book of Hebrews chapter 4 talks about the rest of God. It says, "There remains therefore a rest for the people of God. For he who has entered his rest has himself also cease from his works [music] as God did from his." You see, as long as you are striving, as long as you are walking in your own strength, as long as you are operating in the [music] energy of the flesh, you are not in God's rest. But when you let go, when you cease [music] from your own works, when you stop trying to make things happen in your own wisdom, you enter into a [music] dimension of rest where God begins to work on your behalf. Isaiah 64:4 says, "For since the beginning of the world, men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, nor has the eyes seen any God beside you, who acts for the [music] one who waits for him." God acts for those who wait for him. God [music] moves for those who trust him. God works for those who let go and allow him to take control. I want to prophesy to somebody tonight. You have [music] been struggling. You have been fighting. You have been working so hard trying to make things happen in your own strength. You have been losing sleep. You have been anxious. You have been worried. You have been stressed. But I have come [music] to tell you that your season of struggle is over. Your season of striving is over. The Lord says, "Let go. Surrender that situation to me. Release that burden. Cast that care upon me and watch me turn things around in ways that will shock you." There is a brother or a sister watching me right now and you have been holding on to a business that is failing. You have been pumping in money trying to keep it afloat. You have been working day and night trying to make it succeed. But the Lord is saying to you tonight, if you don't let go, if you don't release it [music] into my hands, you will lose everything. But if you surrender it to me, if you trust [music] me with it, I will either resurrect it or I will give you something better. There is somebody else and you have been holding on to a relationship that God is telling you to let go of. You know in [music] your heart that it is not God's will. You know in your spirit that it is not the right person, but you are afraid of being alone. You are afraid of starting over. You are afraid of letting go. But the Lord is saying to you, as long as you are holding on to the wrong person, you are blocking the right person. As long [music] as you refuse to let go, you are preventing my perfect will from manifesting [music] in your life. The beauty of relying on God is that when you let go, he takes over. When you release your grip, he takes control. When you surrender your will, he releases his power. When you stop trusting in yourself, he begins to move in ways that [music] will amaze you. Let me show you something from the life of Peter. In the Gospel of Luke chapter 5, Jesus had been teaching the people from Peter's boat. When he finished speaking, he said to Peter, "Launch out into [music] the deep and let down your nets for a catch." Now, Peter had been fishing all night and had caught nothing. He was tired. He was disappointed. He was probably frustrated. And [music] here was Jesus, a carpenter, telling him, an expert fisherman, to go back and fish. Peter could have argued. He could have said, "Lord, [music] you don't understand fishing. I've been doing this all my life. I know when the fish bite and when they don't. [music] We've already fished all night in the best conditions and caught nothing." Now, you want [music] us to go out in broad daylight when fishing is even more difficult. But Peter said something beautiful. He said, "Master, we have toiled all night and caught nothing. Nevertheless, at your word, I will let down the net. Nevertheless, at your word, Peter [music] let go of his professional expertise. He let go of his experience. He let go of his natural reasoning. He let go of his logic. And he obeyed the word of Jesus. And when he let down the net, they caught such a great number of fish that their net was breaking. They had to signal to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. and they filled both boats so that they [music] began to sink. This is what happens when you let go of your own understanding and [music] obey God's word. This is what happens when you release your grip on human wisdom and trust in [music] divine instruction. This is what happens when you surrender your way and follow God's way. You don't just get a catch, [music] you get an overflow. You don't just get a blessing, you get abundance. You don't just get [music] provision, you get overflow that you cannot contain. I prophesy to somebody tonight that business that has been struggling. When you let go and surrender it to God, when you start operating by his principles instead of worldly strategies, when you start seeking first his kingdom and his righteousness, God is going to give you such a harvest that you will need help to manage it. that career that has been stagnant. [music] When you stop trying to manipulate and maneuver your way to the top, when you let go and trust God's timing, he's going to promote you in ways that will shock your enemies. Delight yourself also in the Lord and he shall give you the desires of your heart. [music] Commit your way to the Lord. Trust also in him and he shall bring it to pass. Did you see that? Commit your way. Let go of your way and commit to his way. Trust him and he shall bring it to pass. You don't have to [music] make it happen. You don't have to force it.
